cohort: 43 unique guests in guests.json, through Ari Emanuel's October 7, 2026 episode; repeat interviews count once
definition: Employee, apprentice or intern at an organization belonging to someone else before a documented commercial business founding. Student status, investing, mentors and running one's own business do not themselves qualify. Compensation is not always reported. Nonprofit/student organizations are outside the commercial-company definition.
limitations: A confirmed first-company sequence refers to the earliest identifiable commercial business found in the cited histories, not proof that no earlier venture ever existed. Childhood businesses and simultaneous work/startup projects make some sequences unclear. Unclear never means never employed. These are evidence-backed lower bounds within this interview cohort, not population estimates or proof that employment causes founder success.

records.name: Ari Emanuel
records.evidence: Agency employment predates co-founding Endeavor. Informal childhood lawn-mowing is not a separate identifiable company in this classification.

records.name: Jeremy Stern
records.evidence: Guest is Colossus editor-in-chief. No commercial founder role established in this research; do not confuse him with Colossus founder Patrick O'Shaughnessy.

records.name: Alexander Taubman
records.evidence: Describes starting his career at Goldman and then building investment and operating businesses.

records.name: Ronnie Fieg
records.employment: David Z stock boy, salesperson and buyer
records.evidence: Started at David Z at 13 and worked there for approximately 15 years before Kith.

records.name: Peter Rahal
records.employment: Fruit-processing internships, including a placement in Belgium
records.evidence: First-person How I Built This interview describes working in Belgium after graduation, before returning home and starting RXBAR. Not counted merely because his family owned a food business. Founding-year reporting varies between 2012 and 2013; sequence is consistent.

records.name: Luca Ferrari
records.evidence: McKinsey overlaps work on Evertale, so it cannot simply be treated as a job before becoming a founder. It clearly predates Bending Spoons.

records.name: Mati Staniszewski
records.evidence: Official employer biography explicitly places Palantir before ElevenLabs. Student-led Mathscon is not treated as a commercial company.

records.name: Zach Dell
records.evidence: Finance employment predates Base Power, but he had already founded Thread in high school. No earlier employment sequence established.

records.name: Doug Leone
records.evidence: Founder of Sequoia was Don Valentine. Current episode describes Leone returning to Sequoia, not founding a new company at 69. No commercial founder role established here.

records.name: Torsten Reil
records.evidence: Oxford identifies him as a DPhil student when NaturalMotion emerged. Academic research is not automatically employment at someone else's company. Later employment/ownership is not sufficiently separated here.

records.name: Sam Altman
records.evidence: Loopt began while leaving Stanford. A Goldman internship offer was reportedly not taken. An offer, investing and YC leadership after founding Loopt do not establish employment before his first founding.

records.name: Travis Kalanick
records.evidence: Cutco sales precede Uber, but available summaries disagree on dates relative to his teenage SAT-prep business. Conservative first-company classification stays unclear.

records.name: Lulu Cheng Meservey
records.employment: J.P. Morgan financial analyst; World Bank consultant; McLarty adviser
records.evidence: TrailRunner's own biography in its FARA registration lists these earlier roles. Substack/Activision alone would only establish employment before her later company Rostra.

records.name: Michael Ovitz
records.employment: Fox while in college; William Morris trainee and agent
records.evidence: Describes full-time Fox work while at UCLA; William Morris employment also precedes founding CAA.

records.name: Micky Malka
records.evidence: SEC biography establishes co-founding Heptagon at 18. No preceding employee/intern role established. Later investing or CEO roles in his own companies do not qualify.

records.name: David Heinemeier Hansson
records.firstKnownBusiness: Early web projects / Basecamp founder-partner role
records.evidence: Freelance work, early web ventures and joining an existing 37signals partnership need a clearer chronology. Partnership entry is not automatically founding the existing company.

records.name: Jeff Zalaznick
records.firstKnownBusiness: Restaurant websites before Major Food Group
records.employment: J.P. Morgan analyst; Mandarin Oriental employee
records.evidence: Explicit employee-to-entrepreneur chronology before his first restaurant websites, not just before MFG.

records.name: Eric Glyman
records.employment: Houlihan Lokey summer analyst; Millstein financial analyst
records.evidence: Contemporaneous professional biography and dated career history place finance work before Paribus. His student/nonprofit Global China Connection role is outside the commercial-company definition.

records.name: Jonathan Ross
records.evidence: Employer biography explicitly identifies Google work before founding Groq. Creating an internal chip project is not a separate company founding.

records.name: Scott Wu
records.evidence: Episode biography places employee work at Scale AI before co-founding Lunchclub. Founding engineer is an employee role, not assumed to mean company co-founder.

records.name: Steve Stoute
records.employment: Sony and Interscope executive; Arnell Group employee
records.evidence: Strong employment history before Translation, but earliest independent management business and childhood work chronology remain unresolved. Later employment is not proof of employee-first.

records.name: Ed Catmull
records.employment: NYIT researcher; Lucasfilm computer division head
records.evidence: Hired to Lucasfilm in 1979; the division was spun out as Pixar in 1986. An internal research group is not counted as his own commercial company.

records.name: Gustav Soderstrom
records.evidence: Yahoo employment followed his first company. Spotify is not his founding role. The episode summary calls him a 13th Lab co-founder while another biography calls him an adviser, so that later-founder claim is not used in the count.

records.name: Ivanka Trump
records.employment: Forest City Ratner project manager; Trump Organization employee
records.evidence: Employment before launching her own collection is established in contemporary interviews and the episode history.

records.name: Rick Rubin
records.evidence: Started Def Jam from his NYU dorm. No preceding employee role established; making music or recording his own band is not employment evidence.

records.name: Strauss Zelnick
records.employment: Columbia Pictures executive from 1983; later studio/music leadership
records.evidence: Episode biography explicitly places Columbia employment in 1983 and ZMC founding in 2001.

records.name: Dana White
records.evidence: Interviewed former colleague dates bellhop work to 1987, before the boxing business. White did not found the original UFC, which is not the founding anchor used here.

records.name: Adam Foroughi
records.evidence: Episode history places derivatives trading before his two earlier mobile-ad businesses, rather than treating AppLovin as his first founding.

records.name: David Baszucki
records.employment: General Motors engineering internship while at Stanford
records.evidence: GM placement during university predates 1985 graduation and subsequent Knowledge Revolution founding. This record uses a secondary biography and should be upgraded to a direct interview citation when available.

records.name: Evan Spiegel
records.employment: Red Bull and Abraxis BioScience internships in high school; Intuit internship
records.evidence: First-person episode transcript places high-school internships and Intuit before starting Future Freshman with Bobby Murphy, then Snapchat. Earlier company is included rather than treating Snapchat as the first founding.

records.name: Tony Xu
records.employment: Restaurant dishwasher as a child; later professional work
records.evidence: Episode history describes working alongside his mother at a restaurant well before DoorDash. Informal childhood ventures are not treated as separate identifiable companies.

records.name: Marc Andreessen
records.evidence: University Mosaic work and subsequent EIT employment precede Netscape. Mosaic as a university software project is not itself a company founding.

records.name: Brian Armstrong
records.firstKnownBusiness: Tutoring business in college, before Coinbase
records.employment: Airbnb engineer; possible college library work
records.evidence: Airbnb employment clearly predates Coinbase, but he had already run a tutoring business. The library-wage comparison in the transcript is insufficient to establish his own earlier employment chronology.

records.name: Jason Fried
records.evidence: First-person interview gives both first job at 13 and first self-owned entrepreneurial project at approximately 16.

records.name: Jimmy Iovine
records.evidence: Studio employment and engineering work predate his record-label founding. Work with an artist alone is not used as evidence of founding or mentorship.

records.name: Tobi Lutke
records.evidence: German apprenticeship predates moving to Canada in 2002 and Snowdevil in 2004. Count includes apprenticeships, not merely schooling.

records.name: John Mackey
records.employment: Busboy, dishwasher, camp counselor and Good Food store assistant manager
records.evidence: Directly lists pre-founder jobs and the Good Food experience that preceded his own store.

records.name: Patrick O'Shaughnessy
records.firstKnownBusiness: Invest Like the Best / Colossus; Positive Sum
records.evidence: Episode history places OSAM internship before his podcast and media/investment company founding. Employment in a family firm qualifies.

records.name: James Dyson
records.evidence: Official Dyson history explicitly contrasts salaried Rotork work with going independent in 1974.

records.name: Todd Graves
records.evidence: Official company history says these jobs funded the first restaurant.

records.name: Brad Jacobs
records.evidence: Sources establish first founding at 23, but not a prior employee role. Ludwig Jesselson mentorship is not assumed to be employment.

records.name: Michael Dell
records.employment: Restaurant dishwasher from age 12; stamp-store worker; newspaper salesperson
records.evidence: First-person interview establishes childhood jobs before PC's Limited. Ordering versus earliest childhood stamp-selling ventures is unresolved.

records.name: Daniel Ek
records.employment: Tradera and Stardoll roles before Spotify
records.evidence: Had already founded a web business before adult employment. Founding ages vary in sources, but neither supports employment before that first business.
